kjv: A Syrian ready to perish [was] my father
mine: My father was a wandering Aramean
note: Hebrew 'arammi 'oved 'avi: 'oved can mean "perishing" or "straying, wandering" (of lost sheep), and the context (going down to Egypt as a sojourner) favours a homeless wanderer, i.e. Jacob; "Syrian" is an anachronistic label for Aram. Context: wandering (medium confidence). 'Oved means 'perishing, lost, straying' (of strayed animals, Deut 22:3; Jer 50:6). With 'he went down to Egypt and lived there as a foreigner' it describes Jacob as a homeless, endangered migrant. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and CSB read 'wandering', NJPS 'fugitive'; 'wandering' loses some of the sense of danger. Other possible meanings: (1) 'ready to perish' or 'starving' — KJV, several lexicons and medieval commentators (Ibn Ezra); (2) 'an Aramean (Laban) sought to destroy my father', reading 'oved as causative — Targum Onqelos, the Passover Haggadah, Rashi, Vulgate (persequebatur); (3) 'fugitive' — NJPS.

kjv: neither have I taken away [ought] thereof (the holy portion) for [any] unclean [use]
mine: nor removed any of it (the holy portion) while unclean
note: Hebrew bitame' most naturally means "in a state of uncleanness" (parallel to be'oni, "in my mourning"); the KJV's supplied "use" shifts the uncleanness from the offerer to the purpose.

kjv: Thou (Israel) hast avouched the LORD this day
mine: You (Israel) have declared today that Yahweh is your God
note: Hebrew he'emarta (a rare hiphil of 'amar) means "you have caused to say / declared, affirmed" in a covenant exchange; "avouched" is obsolete.
